coverage_gaps: Only PubMed was available; dedicated citation graphs and DOI metadata services were unavailable, so forward-citation and study-family expansion may be incomplete.

Dedicated human-genetics sources such as GWAS Catalog, ClinVar, locus-specific databases, and population-frequency resources were unavailable, limiting independent variant-annotation and ancestry-frequency verification.
Preprint servers were unavailable, so unreviewed findings available by 2024-12-31 may be absent.
Trial registries and regulator sources were unavailable, limiting independent assessment of ongoing LRRK2 inhibitor studies and regulatory safety context.
PubMed indexing and abstract availability can omit non-indexed literature, conference material, full experimental detail, and some corrections or retractions.
exclusion_criteria: Records published after 2024-12-31 are excluded from the evidence set and logged for a future update.
Records mentioning LRRK2 or Parkinson disease without substantive genetic, enzymatic, substrate, physiological, or limitation evidence are excluded.
Purely computational docking, unvalidated prediction, commentary, news, and hypothesis-only records are excluded from primary mechanistic support.
Non-Parkinson LRRK2 studies are excluded unless they directly establish transferable enzymatic, substrate, or physiological evidence and their disease-context limitation can be stated.
Studies using only overexpression, nonphysiological substrate concentrations, or surrogate phosphorylation markers without orthogonal validation cannot support a physiological-substrate designation.
Duplicate reports are excluded as separate evidence units after canonicalization, while distinct cohorts, experiments, follow-ups, corrections, and query-hit links are retained.
Records with inaccessible language or insufficient methods and results for reliable assessment are excluded from claim support and recorded as an access limitation.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31; ambiguous online-first, issue, and correction dates are retained for explicit date adjudication.
Human linkage, segregation, population association, genome-wide association, founder, ancestry, or penetrance evidence that directly evaluates LRRK2 in Parkinson disease or parkinsonism is eligible.

Biochemical, structural, cellular, human-tissue, or animal studies are eligible when they directly test LRRK2 kinase or ROC-COR GTPase activity, variant effects, substrate phosphorylation, or resulting physiology.

A protein is described as a physiological substrate only when direct phosphorylation evidence is paired with endogenous, inhibitor-sensitive, genetic-perturbation, tissue, or in-vivo support; weaker candidates remain labeled by assay context.
Null, negative, conflicting, replication, correction, retraction, incomplete-penetrance, and population- or model-specific evidence is retained when it constrains a major claim.
Reviews and meta-analyses are eligible for terminology, study-family mapping, and citation expansion; mechanistic claims in the final brief require verification against primary records.
All organisms and languages are eligible when the record supplies enough translated text and methodological detail for reliable screening and extraction.
Records are deduplicated by PMID, DOI, and study identity while every query-to-record occurrence and publication-version relationship is preserved.

queries.purpose: Recover the 2004 PARK8/LRRK2 discovery reports and early pathogenic-variant anchors while validating gene, historical locus, disease, author, and variant terminology.
queries.query: ((LRRK2[Title/Abstract] OR PARK8[Title/Abstract] OR dardarin[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Parkinson Disease"[MeSH Terms] OR "Parkinson disease"[Title/Abstract] OR parkinsonism[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Zimprich A"[Author] OR "Paisan-Ruiz C"[Author] OR G2019S[Title/Abstract] OR R1441C[Title/Abstract])) AND ("1900/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: from the earliest PubMed-indexed literature through 2024-12-31, determine how human genetic discovery and disease-associated LRRK2 variants connect Parkinson disease to LRRK2 kinase and ROC-COR GTPase biology; identify direct physiological substrates and downstream cellular consequences; and assess penetrance, ancestry, model-system, variant-specific, null, conflicting, correction, and retraction evidence that limits causal or mechanistic generalization. Human studies anchor disease association, while human tissue and cells, animal models, and purified systems inform mechanism. All languages are eligible when sufficient translated text is available for assessment.
stop_rules: Complete all 12 preregistered PubMed query events, including sentinel, discovery, confirmation, expansion, challenge, and update waves.

Confirm recovery of the 2004 PARK8/LRRK2 genetic-discovery anchors, an early recurrent G2019S report, and the phosphoproteomic Rab-substrate anchor; revise terminology within the 12-event budget if any anchor is missed.

Stop iterative expansion after two consecutive completed expansion or confirmation passes add no decision-relevant genetic variant, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrate, or limiting evidence after deduplication.

Require primary evidence for genetic discovery, pathogenic and risk variants, kinase and GTPase mechanism, physiological substrates, and at least one material limitation before declaring thematic saturation.
Stop when newly retrieved records only duplicate established study families or add detail that cannot alter the brief's calibrated conclusions.
Stop at the hard maximum of 12 query events and report any unresolved theme, anchor miss, or source-class deficit as a coverage gap.
Apply the publication cutoff after retrieval when PubMed date semantics are ambiguous and stop the update wave only after all eligible records through 2024-12-31 have been adjudicated.
